newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Cuban cruise ship cancels Cayman Brac port of call.
newsitem.headline: Cuban cruise ship cancels Cayman Brac port of call.

text.p: The Cuban-based cruise ship Melia Don Juan will end its weekly stop at Cayman Brac island at the end of this month, officials in both the Cayman government and the Spanish company that operates the cruise ship said Thursday.
The cancellation notice comes two months before the end of a six-month trial period for the cruises.
But the ship will continue its weekly stop at Grand Cayman, the largest island in the British colony.
A spokesman for the Cayman government said the weekly cruise to Cayman Brac was cancelled because of a "pattern of bad weather" that prevented the ship from anchoring offshore on several occasions.

Ricard Linares, a spokesman for the Melia Hotel Co of Madrid that operates the ship out of Cienfuegos, Cuba, said the ship would end its visits to Cayman Brac, the second largest island in the territory, on Feb. 28.
Store owners on Cayman Brac said privately that the 458-person capacity cruise ship rarely brought more than 60 passengers to the island, and few of the tourists spent much money.

The Melia Hotel chain operates several beach resorts in Cuba and has been trying to attract upscale vacationers from Europe, Canada and South America. Cuban citizens are not allowed to sail on the cruises.
